title: Tuning Wettability of Manganese Oxide Nanostructures by Controlled Morphology Modification
content: Manganese oxide (MO) nanostructures have attracted significant attention due to their versatile applications, such as in energy storage [1, 2], catalysis [3], and sensors [4]. Among their various properties, the wettability of MO nanostructures is particularly important, as it can significantly influence material performance [5]. Wettability is closely related to surface conditions, such as morphology and roughness. For example, hierarchical structures with multiscale roughness often result in superhydrophobic surfaces, as observed in lotus leaves. Therefore, precise control over morphology is essential for tunning wettability to meet specific application requirements. In this study, we investigate the wetting properties of MO nanostructures through controlled morphology modification.
